name: AI Agent Config
desc: A set of rules for coding agents that lives in one place and gets rendered into the instruction file each tool reads.

p: Every coding agent looks for its own instruction file, and copies of those files drift apart as they move between repositories. AI Agent Config keeps the durable rules in one provider-neutral place and generates the files from them. It runs on Python's standard library, so it needs no paid subscription or specific model.
Adapters exist for Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Google Antigravity and a generic entry point.

A universal core holds the contract and names no provider. A project adds its own rules and an overlay for its type, and an adapter renders the selected result into the file that tool reads, such as AGENTS.md for Codex, CLAUDE.md for Claude Code or GEMINI.md for Gemini CLI. Validate checks the source first, then diff shows what would change in the target before anything is installed.

Guided setup asks for the provider and the project, then installs one generated file after you confirm. It doesn't replace an existing provider file silently. A doctor command checks later that the installed file still matches the current rules.

Setup comes in four modes, from a bare baseline to agent-heavy projects with delegation and deeper review. Personal preferences sit in an optional private profile that ranks below the project's rules.
